assumptions.text: Every device-originated packet must carry a device credential proof because the inputs state security is required and device authentication is unspecified.
assumptions.excludes: Anonymous or network-location-based acceptance of ingress packets.

assumptions.text: The in-process publisher of validated events is treated as an internal service principal that is attributed to the downstream event streams boundary.
assumptions.excludes: Accepting events on the consumer surface from any caller that is not the trusted publisher.

assumptions.text: No tenant concept is declared, so the device identity bound to the credential is the single ownership scope for ingested records.
Telemetry samples are health-related data of an athlete and are classified as confidential personal data.
assumptions.excludes: Treating raw samples as public or internal data.

trust_boundaries.name: Service to logs, metrics and error responses

data_classification.retention: Retain append-only history for the period the platform requires and no longer.
data_classification.deletion: Erase an athlete's records on verified request by an operator-controlled process that is itself audited.
data_classification.reason: Physiological samples tied to a device identify an athlete's health data.

data_classification.retention: Retain with the record it revises.
data_classification.deletion: Erase together with the record it revises.
data_classification.reason: A revision carries the same health values as the record it corrects.

data_classification.retention: Retain for the audit period and never mutate.
data_classification.deletion: Delete only by expiry of the audit period.
data_classification.reason: Audit entries name actors and actions but carry no sample values.

data_classification.retention: Hold only in bounded in-memory windows and discard on broadcast or overflow.
data_classification.deletion: Discard on window expiry because the buffer is non-authoritative.
data_classification.reason: Authenticated analytics consumers must receive sample values to fulfil the broadcast purpose.

authorization_matrix.test_duty: Permitted: a credentialed device appends its own samples; denied: a packet without a valid credential is rejected; cross-owner: a valid device posting samples naming another device_id is refused.

authorization_matrix.ownership_rule: Accept an event only from the trusted publisher and only for a device_id, metric, t_device and revision it identifies in its own versioned event.
authorization_matrix.test_duty: Permitted: a versioned event from the trusted publisher is buffered; denied: an event from an unknown caller is dropped; cross-owner: an event whose identity does not match its payload device_id is refused.

Permitted: an authenticated consumer with the subscribe scope receives windows; denied: an unauthenticated or unscoped subscriber receives nothing; cross-owner: a consumer lacking the scope is refused identically to a missing one.

invariants.rule: A packet is never accepted unless the device credential proof verifies, and an unavailable verifier denies.
invariants.verification: A packet sent with an expired, revoked or absent credential is stored.

invariants.rule: The device_id of every stored sample always equals the identity bound to the verified credential and is never taken from the payload alone.
invariants.verification: A record exists whose device_id differs from the authenticated device of its request.

invariants.rule: Every packet is validated and typed at the edge before deeper layers receive it, and oversized or malformed packets are rejected.
invariants.verification: A malformed or oversized packet reaches the application layer untyped.

invariants.rule: Raw records, revisions and audit entries are never updated or deleted by the service principal.
invariants.verification: An update or delete statement by the service credential succeeds on a stored row.

invariants.rule: Stored telemetry is always protected at rest and in transit as classified.
invariants.verification: A stored sample value is readable from the store without the data key.

invariants.rule: Distribution never accepts an event that is not versioned and from the trusted publisher.
invariants.verification: An unversioned or foreign event is buffered into a window.

invariants.rule: A broadcast stream is never opened without a verified consumer credential and the subscribe scope.
invariants.verification: A subscription without a client certificate receives any window.

invariants.rule: Logs never contain sample values, payloads or device identifiers and error responses carry only code, message and correlation key.
invariants.verification: A log line or error body contains a sample value, payload or device_id.

invariants.rule: Metric tags are always drawn from bounded enumerations and never carry identifiers.
invariants.verification: A metric series exists whose tag value is a device identifier.

invariants.rule: Authentication failures, authorization denials and service credential use always emit a security audit event.
invariants.verification: A denied request leaves no audit entry with its correlation key.

inventory.name: device-credential-verification-material
inventory.rotation: Rotate on a fixed schedule and revoke on device loss with revocation failing closed.

inventory.name: data-encryption-key
inventory.rotation: Rotate on a fixed schedule with key access held apart from data access.

inventory.name: consumer-certificate-trust-anchor
inventory.rotation: Rotate before expiry with revocation failing closed.

handling_rules: Secrets are supplied at runtime and never persisted in plain form.
Key access is separated from data access.
Credential lifetime, renewal, revocation and clock-skew tolerance are bounded and revocation fails closed.

duties.obligation: Authenticate the device, require the ingest scope and bind device_id to the credential before accepting any packet.
Refuse any packet whose device_id differs from the authenticated device with a response that never reveals existence.
Accept validated events only from the trusted publisher and drop all others with an audit event.
Require a verified consumer certificate and the subscribe scope before opening a stream.
Deny every packet when credential verification fails or the verifier is unavailable.
Derive the stored device_id from the verified identity and compare it with the payload value.
Convert each packet to typed values with size and shape limits at the receiving boundary.
Grant the service principal insert and read rights only on records, revisions and audit entries.
Protect stored samples with envelope protection under a key held apart from data access.
Deserialize only versioned events into typed values and reject any other shape.
Verify the consumer credential before any subscription is established.
Redact sample values, payloads and device identifiers from logs and return only code, message and correlation key in errors.
Restrict metric tags to bounded enumerations and reject identifier-valued tags.
Record an audit event for each authentication failure, authorization denial and service credential use.
Apply the confidential personal-data classification to records for storage, logs, errors and exports.
Apply the confidential personal-data classification to revisions for storage, logs, errors and exports.
Keep audit entries free of sample values and append-only.
Hold broadcast windows only in bounded memory and keep their content out of logs and errors.

risks.risk: Device authentication is unspecified in the inputs, so the credential scheme may be unsupported by existing devices.
risks.mitigation: AZ-01 and SI-01 require a device credential proof and deny on failure.
risks.residual: operator: devices that cannot present a credential cannot ingest until the operator provisions one.

risks.risk: Any authenticated analytics consumer receives every device's windows because no per-consumer ownership is declared.
risks.mitigation: AZ-03 limits the stream to credentialed, scoped consumers.
risks.residual: accepted: a scoped consumer sees all devices' windows until a consumer-to-device relation is declared.

risks.risk: A packet later than the 60 second window is handled without a decided policy and might be mis-recorded.
risks.mitigation: SI-04 keeps the record append-only so any late packet is preserved as a revision.
risks.residual: accepted: the late-packet disposition stays undecided pending the operator's confirmation.

risks.risk: Unbounded packet volume could exhaust the ingress path.
risks.mitigation: SI-03 rejects oversized or malformed packets at the edge.
risks.residual: operator: rate limiting of authenticated devices is not specified in the inputs.
